subagent_reports.architecture_assessment: Target: separate durable read store from Temporal command authority. Read tools load bounded typed projections with version tokens; Temporal Queries remain diagnostics/reconciliation only. Commands use a receipt/idempotency key and must not report success until an idempotent, revision-conditional projection write has completed and been read back. Current workflow-side projection scheduling is explicitly fire-and-forget (workflows.ts:977-985), so it cannot meet that success guarantee without redesign. The local projection transaction already supplies the right atomic/readback primitive (change-projection-transaction.ts:90-104,225-260).

validation.notes: Direction is sound, but long-term success semantics require replacing fire-and-forget workflow projection scheduling with a command/projection acknowledgement protocol. Packet omitted TASK_SCOPE, IN_SCOPE, OUT_OF_SCOPE, DONE_WHEN, STOP_WHEN, and VERIFICATION anchors; report uses supplied user scope.

tradeoffs: External projections add schema, migration, repair, and convergence obligations.
Synchronous command acknowledgement increases mutation latency but makes read-your-write and success semantics explicit.
Temporal remains necessary for durable command ordering, workflow recovery, and lifecycle, but no longer scales with read fan-out.

alternatives_considered.option: Keep routine reads as Temporal Queries and raise worker capacity
alternatives_considered.rationale: Queries are workflow/worker-dependent synchronous reads; capacity only masks N×session fan-out and poisoned/orphaned workflow failure modes.

alternatives_considered.option: Disk-first reads with post-mutation query plus caller-side write-through
alternatives_considered.rationale: Matches existing durable transaction and minimizes current issue, but its fire-and-forget workflow projection path and query dependency cannot give durable read-model acknowledgement uniformly.

alternatives_considered.option: Move all mutable state from Temporal to the read store
alternatives_considered.rationale: Would discard Temporal's durable command ordering and recovery value; command and read stores should have distinct responsibilities.

alternatives_considered.option: Use Temporal Updates for every synchronous externally-observable command
alternatives_considered.rationale: Official docs define Updates as trackable synchronous workflow mutations; pair them with idempotent projection activity completion before returning success.

architecture_judgement.recommendation: Ship present disk-first read flip as short-term bridge, then create dedicated command/read-store split change: durable projections become routine read authority; Updates/receipts plus awaited idempotent projection activities establish command success; Queries become bounded diagnostic reconciliation only.

subagent_reports.recommendation: Recommended target and sequence: (1) finish KD1/KD2/KD3 disk-first bridge and typed not-found; retain Temporal-fresh post-mutation readbacks. (2) Define one projection envelope per entity: schemaVersion, entityId, projectionRevision, commandId/receipt, lifecycle, source status, and typed not_found/degraded results. (3) Move all routine reads—changes/tasks/gates/wisdom/deltas/epics—to projection indexes/snapshots; static catalogs/spec catalog remain pure file/registry reads with zero Temporal. (4) Introduce idempotent command updates with stable command IDs; reducer applies/records receipt, serializes conflicting commands, awaits conditional projection activity, and returns only verified projection revision. Signals remain async/internal/best-effort only. (5) Keep Query/Describe/Visibility for repair, liveness, migration, and bounded reconcile; never require per-entity Query to render normal reads. (6) Complete terminal workflows after projection/archive proof; Continue-As-New active entities at server suggestion/history threshold and persist dedupe ledger/seed state. Use patching or Worker Versioning for workflow-code command changes. (7) Add reconciler/repair for missing, poisoned, orphaned workflows: projection read still succeeds with degraded provenance; mutation returns typed operator-required or recovery path, never silently re-seeds on an unknown query failure. D1/KD1 immediate disk return best aligns. D2/KD2 typed not-found required target API behavior. D3/KD3 shared sibling primitive aligns only if it evolves into projection-store API rather than permanent Temporal-shaped abstraction.

requirement.body: ADV state-changing commands must carry stable operation identity, be validated and applied by the authoritative Temporal workflow reducer, and return success only after the accepted monotonic state revision is committed to and verified in the durable projection. Routine read state must never authorize a mutation. Signal-based command confirmation may use a bounded workflow Query; routine reads may not.

The durable summary shard points to the same state revision

scenarios.title: Projection failure prevents false success

The operation id and accepted revision support deterministic repair without blind retry

documents.proposal:
# Finish disk-first active reads

## Why

ADV routine reads still depend on synchronous Temporal workflow Queries. Under multi-session load, missing/poisoned workflows, orphaned task queues, or a dead worker, read tools time out or surface infrastructure errors even though durable state already exists outside the workflow.

The first design proposed globally flipping `getTemporalChange` to disk-primary. Independent validation rejected that approach: not every mutation synchronously projects state, some projections are fire-and-forget, and lifecycle authorization such as close/closeBatch still depends on workflow-fresh preflight state. Disk presence alone therefore cannot prove freshness or authorization safety.

The durable solution is projection-first CQRS-lite: Temporal remains the command-ordering and reducer authority; a versioned external projection becomes the routine read model; command success includes proof that the accepted workflow revision was durably projected.

## Root Cause Analysis

Defect origin. ADV uses the workflow worker as both command processor and read database. Routine reads consume workflow-task capacity, require replayability/poller availability, and share failure modes with command execution. Projection writes are inconsistent: some mutation paths synchronously call `persistStateToDiskDurable`, while others schedule best-effort projection or only invalidate cache. Lifecycle authorization is also partly host-preflight-owned instead of reducer-owned.

Evidence:
- `getTemporalChange` loads disk then still always queries the workflow (`store-temporal/index.ts:882-924`).
- Worker workflow-task concurrency defaults to 4 (`temporal/worker-tuning.ts:47-51`).
- Atomic conditional projection machinery already exists (`change-projection-transaction.ts`).
- Fire-and-forget projection exists in workflow signal handling (`workflows.ts:949-985`).
- `changes.close` / `closeBatch` authorize from `getTemporalChange`, while close reducer handling lacks equivalent lifecycle validation.
- Tool catalog/describe already demonstrate the correct pure, Temporal-free shape (`tool-catalog-entries.ts`, `tool-registry.ts:1127-1226`).

## What Changes

1. Introduce structurally separate read and command contracts: `ReadStore` for projection snapshots; `CommandStore` for Temporal-backed mutations.
2. Add monotonic state/projection revision and stable command/operation identity. Every accepted state-changing command increments revision.
3. Tighten command success: Signal → bounded command-confirmation Query → atomic conditional projection commit → readback verification → success with acknowledged revision. Projection failure returns typed ambiguous/not-durable outcome, never false success.
4. Move lifecycle authorization into workflow reducers, beginning with close/closeBatch, so stale advisory preflight cannot authorize invalid mutations.
5. Route routine dynamic reads (change/task/gate/wisdom/delta/Epic/status/WIP) through the projection read model. Missing/poisoned/orphaned workflows do not affect these reads.
6. Add a durable summary index so default list/status reads do not hydrate every full change (`rq-changeSummaryReadModel01`).
7. Keep Queries only for command confirmation, reconciliation, diagnostics, and repair. Routine reads issue zero workflow Queries.
8. Keep pure/static surfaces (tool catalog/describe, specs, project context) outside both Temporal and entity projection machinery.

## User Outcomes

- Read tools remain available when Temporal workers are down, workflows are poisoned, or session queues are orphaned.
- Missing entities return typed not-found, not `ServiceError / Failed to query Workflow`.
- Mutation success means workflow state and durable projection agree at a specific monotonic revision.
- Status/list reads scale with disk/index I/O, not number of active workflows or concurrent sessions.
- Tool catalog and other static registries remain instant and Temporal-independent.

## Scope

### In Scope
- Typed projection snapshot/read contract and ReadStore/CommandStore separation.
- Monotonic revision/command receipt persisted in workflow state and disk projection.
- Synchronous projection-proof contract for successful mutations exposed by migrated read surfaces.
- Reducer-owned lifecycle authorization for close/closeBatch.
- Projection-backed change/task/gate/wisdom/delta/Epic/status/WIP reads.
- Durable summary index for default list/status reads.
- Typed not-found/degraded outcomes.
- Tier-4 classifications separating `needs-read-model` from Temporal diagnostics.

### Out of Scope
- New database: filesystem projection remains the initial read-model backend.
- Workflow retirement/Continue-As-New/Signal-With-Start lifecycle work (`bl-MsU7dzK0`, independent companion concern).
- Replacing Signals with Temporal Updates (`defineUpdate` remains forbidden by project workflow-surface policy).
- Raising worker slot or poller caps.

### Must Not
- Return command success before projection revision is durably verified.
- Use wall-clock time as freshness authority.
- Use projection/read-model state as final mutation authorization.
- Route pure catalog/spec/context reads through Temporal.
- Preserve mandatory workflow Queries in routine read tools.

## Affected Capabilities and Draft Spec Obligation

- `advance-workflow`: command acknowledgement + projection revision + reducer authority + routine-read Query prohibition.
- `advance-meta`: durable summary read model and Tier-4 read classification.
- Draft requirements must cover projection-backed reads, revision proof, typed not-found/degraded outcomes, reducer-owned lifecycle authorization, and zero routine Query calls.

## Discovery Basis

- Independent validator verdict: CONFLICT on global disk-presence-as-freshness.
- Long-term architecture research: CQRS-lite with external projection and Temporal command plane.
- Local precedents: `commitChangeProjection`, `launcher-projection.ts`, `shared/cli-projection.ts`, `cli/projection-boundary.ts`, pure tool catalog registry, and `Store.changes.listSummary`.

# Problem: per-change ADV reads still treat the Temporal workflow as the read database

## Symptom (live, observed 2026-07-26)

- `adv_change_show fixOpsResolutionProjection` (a non-existent change id) returns `ServiceError / Failed to query Workflow` instead of a typed not-found from disk.
- `adv_epic_show hardenTemporalReliability view:full` hits the 10s `ToolExecutionTimeout`.
- `adv_worktree_triage` reports 4 changes (`fixDirectArchiveRetry`, `fixReviewerEvidence`, `hardenWorkflowRecovery`, `optimizeCiWaiter`) failing worktree-registry snapshot queries with `FAILED_PRECONDITION: no poller seen for task queue recently`.

All three are read paths that should never depend on a worker round-trip for state the system already has on disk.

## Defect origin

Unintended behavior: per-change and per-epic reads route through synchronous Temporal workflow Queries even when a fresh durable disk projection exists. Under multi-session load, on orphaned session queues, or against missing/poisoned workflows, these queries fail or hang and surface as infrastructure-shaped errors instead of disk reads.

## Root Cause Analysis

**Leading hypothesis (high confidence, code-verified):** ADV's read model is half-flipped. The list/enumeration path is disk-first; the per-change path is not.

### Evidence gathered

**Tier 1 — local code (verified 2026-07-26):**

- `plugin/src/temporal/worker-tuning.ts:47-51` — `maxConcurrentWorkflowTaskExecutions` defaults to **4** (env `ADV_WORKER_WORKFLOW_SLOT_CAP`). Every read Query consumes one slot.
- `plugin/src/storage/store-temporal/index.ts:1426-1490` — `listResolvedChanges` IS disk-first (tagged `bl-HiZJbUuy / disk-authoritative active reads`): loads `legacy.changes.get(changeId)` from disk before any workflow query; query is a fall-through on disk miss.
- `plugin/src/storage/store-temporal/index.ts:882-995` — `getTemporalChange` is NOT disk-first. It does Leg A (disk load) + Leg B (workflow Query at 1500ms cap). **Leg B always runs** — disk only wins on circuit-breaker trip, `workflow_unresponsive`, or `missing_workflow` recovery. The query is the authoritative read; disk is a fallback cache. Used by every per-change read: `adv_change_show`, `adv_gate_status`, `adv_task_list/show`, `adv_wisdom_list`, `adv_delta_*`, `adv_spec` change-scoped, `_adapters.ts`, `verification-evidence.ts`, `contract.ts`.
- Sibling read modules call `.query(changeStateQuery)` directly with no disk-first path:
  - `tasks.ts` — 5 sites (lines 48, 89, 131, 185, 217) + 3 variant sites (35, 144, 154)
  - `gates.ts` — 3 sites (71, 173, 208)
  - `wisdom.ts` — 2 sites (52, 69)
  - `spec-deltas.ts` — 6 sites (79, 119, 160, 200, 239, 279)
- `plugin/src/storage/store-temporal/index.ts:1020-1033` — terminal `change.json` (archived OR closed) IS disk-authoritative. The exact precedence the per-change path needs is already proven for terminal state.

**Tier 2 — external (Temporal semantics):**

- A workflow Query is a synchronous worker round-trip requiring sticky-cache or full-history replay. The SDK guarantees neither is free.
- `read-context.test.ts:399` documents the read shape: "one visibility-list RPC plus one query per change." N workflows × M sessions against 4 worker slots ⇒ `SOURCE_DEADLINE_EXCEEDED` at the 8s aggregate read budget.
- Workflows on orphaned session queues (started by dead sessions, sitting on `advance-{P}-{sessionId}` queues no live worker polls) fail `FAILED_PRECONDITION: no poller seen for task queue recently`. Verified live in this session's `adv_worktree_triage`.

**Tier 3 — prior art (in-repo):**

- `makeReadsDiskAuthoritative` (archived 2026-07-23, commit `1879fb64`) added the circuit-breaker + 1500ms cap + bounded-enrichment layer. Its executive summary states the scope: "query demoted to bounded enrichment." It did NOT make the query optional. Its reviewer findings explicitly flagged the epic-list gap (shipped via `addEpicListCircuitBreaker`, `7de2cd0b`) and the `probe_degraded` inverse concern (`fixHealthDegradedAlive`).
- `isolateAdvWorkerTaskQueues` (per-session task-queue routing) did not and cannot fix this — it changed signal routing, not the Query-first read model, and introduced the orphaned-session-queue amplifier.

### Ruled-out paths

- Raising `ADV_WORKER_WORKFLOW_SLOT_CAP` — fights the multi-session poller-footprint budget (`rq-isolSessionTaskQueue03`/AC7 = 18 pollers cap). The fix is to stop sending reads to the worker, not to make the worker survive more read load.
- `makeReadsDiskAuthoritative` CB layer as the complete fix — today's symptoms disprove it. It prevents hangs; it does not prevent load or missing-workflow errors.
- Per-session queue isolation — orthogonal; addresses signal routing, not read precedence.

### Spec-law impact

Durable change required. `advance-workflow` v1.39.0 covers read tools but does not currently state a disk-first read-precedence invariant for active/non-terminal changes. The terminal-state disk-authoritative rule (`rq-terminalProjectionTruth01`, `rq-archiveRetirement01.1`) is established; this extends the same precedence to active state with a monotonic-freshness reconcile contract.

# Agreement: Projection-first ADV reads

## Objectives

- OBJ1: Temporal workflows own command ordering, reducer validation, idempotency, and command receipts; they do not serve routine reads.
- OBJ2: A versioned external projection is the primary read model for changes, tasks, gates, wisdom, deltas, Epics, status, and WIP.
- OBJ3: Every successful state-changing command proves its accepted workflow revision was atomically committed and verified in the projection.
- OBJ4: Lifecycle authorization is structurally enforced in workflow reducers; host preflight is advisory only.
- OBJ5: Pure metadata surfaces such as tool catalog/describe, specs, and project context remain Temporal-free.

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC1: A schema-validated `ReadSnapshot<T>` represents found, typed not-found, revision, source, and degraded provenance without exposing mutation authority.
- AC2: Read and command contracts are structurally separated. Routine read tools compile against `ReadStore`; mutation tools use `CommandStore`/Temporal command adapters.
- AC3: Every accepted behavior-changing command carries a stable operation ID and increments a monotonic state revision mirrored in the disk projection.
- AC4: A command returns success only after `commitChangeProjection` (or its canonical wrapper) atomically commits and readback-verifies `projection.revision >= acknowledgedRevision`. Injected projection failure cannot return success and produces a typed non-blind-retry outcome.
- AC5: close/closeBatch lifecycle eligibility is validated by the workflow reducer. A stale host preflight cannot close an archived, closed, or otherwise ineligible change.
- AC6: `adv_change_show`, gate/task/wisdom/delta/Epic read tools, default `adv_status`, and `adv_wip_state` return from the read model with zero workflow Query calls when projection exists.
- AC7: Missing workflow + present projection returns a normal snapshot; poisoned/orphaned workflow + present projection returns a normal or degraded snapshot; missing workflow + missing projection returns typed not-found.
- AC8: Default `adv_change_list` and warm/default `adv_status` use a durable summary index and do not hydrate every full change when summary fields satisfy the response.
- AC9: Workflow Queries are structurally prohibited from routine read adapters. They remain allowed only for bounded command confirmation, reconciliation, diagnostics, and repair.
- AC10: `adv_tool_catalog` and `adv_tool_describe` remain pure in-memory registry reads with no Store or Temporal requirement; specs/project context remain direct context/file reads.
- AC11: Tier-4 read classification distinguishes `needs-read-model` from `needs-temporal-diagnostics`; read-model-backed tools degrade by provenance rather than failing on Temporal reachability.
- AC12: Existing post-signal mutation safety (`outcome_unknown_readback_unavailable`, idempotency, no blind retry) and terminal projection dominance remain intact.
- AC13: Workflow bundle boundary and replay tests pass; revision/reducer changes have worker-bundle build and replay-determinism evidence before release.

## Constraints

- C1: Signals remain the workflow command surface; do not introduce `defineUpdate`.
- C2: Filesystem projection is the initial backend; do not add a database unless evidence proves the transactional projection cannot meet the contract.
- C3: Freshness authority is monotonic revision/receipt, never wall-clock time.
- C4: Command confirmation Query volume is acceptable; routine read Query volume must be zero.
- C5: `commitChangeProjection` remains the canonical atomic conditional writer; no parallel persistence primitive.
- C6: Read-model snapshots cannot authorize gates, archive, close, task completion, claims, worker recovery, or contract evidence.
- C7: Worker slot/poller caps remain unchanged.
- C8: Existing `source`/degraded response consumers receive a compatible migration path.

## Avoidances

- AVOID1: Do not globally flip `getTemporalChange` based only on disk presence.
- AVOID2: Do not return success from fire-and-forget projection scheduling.
- AVOID3: Do not keep mixed read semantics hidden behind a permanent `readOnly` flag on a command-oriented getter.
- AVOID4: Do not move static catalogs into entity projection or Temporal.
- AVOID5: Do not infer authorization from stale projections; reducer validation is mandatory.
- AVOID6: Do not raise worker capacity to mask routine read amplification.
- AVOID7: Do not bundle independent workflow-history retirement mechanics into this read-model contract.

## Out of Scope

- Continue-As-New thresholds, dormant workflow hibernation, terminal workflow retirement, and Worker Versioning rollout policy beyond required replay/build evidence.
- Replacing Signal-based command protocol with Temporal Updates.

# Design: Projection-first CQRS-lite

## Architecture

ADV separates four planes:

1. **Pure metadata** — tool catalog/describe, specs, backlog, project context. Registry/files only.
2. **Read model** — schema-versioned full snapshots and durable per-entity summary shards for routine reads.
3. **Command plane** — Signal-based Temporal commands, reducer authorization, stable operation identity, bounded confirmation Query, projection proof.
4. **Operational plane** — Visibility, Describe, health probes, reconciliation, repair.

Routine tools never cross from read plane into command/operational plane.

## Core Contracts

```ts
type ProjectionRevision = number;
type StateRevision = number;
type OperationId = string;

type ReadSnapshot<T> =
  | {
      found: true;
      snapshot: T;
      stateRevision: StateRevision;
      projectionRevision: ProjectionRevision;
      source: "read_model";
      degraded?: { reason: string };
    }
  | { found: false; reason: "not_found"; source: "read_model" };

interface ReadStore { /* change/task/gate/wisdom/delta/Epic/summary reads */ }
interface CommandStore { /* Temporal-backed mutations only */ }
```

Read types expose no command handle or authorization result.

## Stable Operation Ledger

Replace retry-local receipt IDs (`Date.now()` + `Math.random()`) with caller-supplied `operation_id`, generated once at the tool-command boundary and reused by every retry/recovery attempt.

Workflow state gains a bounded ledger:

```ts
interface OperationLedgerEntry {
  operation_id: string;
  command_kind: string;
  payload_hash: string;
  outcome: "accepted" | "rejected" | "idempotent_replay";
  state_revision: number;
  rejection_code?: string;
}
```

- Same ID + same payload returns prior result without reducer reapplication/revision increment.
- Same ID + different payload is a typed conflict.
- Deterministic bounded retention covers supported retry horizon and survives Continue-As-New.
- Confirmation Query returns the full matching ledger entry.

## State Revision

Add optional `state_revision` to workflow and projection schemas.

- Legacy/absent = 0.
- Accepted behavior-changing reducer transition increments exactly once.
- Rejection/idempotent replay does not increment.
- Seed and Continue-As-New preserve revision and ledger.
- Full snapshot and summary shard carry identical state revision.

New command-producing branches/activity scheduling on existing histories use `wf.patched()` then `wf.deprecatePatch()`. Worker-bundle build and replay tests are mandatory.

## Command Success Protocol

Signals remain the command surface; `defineUpdate` remains forbidden.

```text
1. Generate/reuse stable operation_id + payload hash.
2. Signal workflow.
3. Run bounded confirmation Query for ledger entry.
4. Rejection → typed reducer rejection.
5. Acceptance/idempotent replay → obtain confirmed state_revision/state.
6. Commit full snapshot + summary shard with revision/operation fences.
7. Read back both and verify acknowledged revision/operation.
8. Return success + acknowledged revision.
```

Allowed Query categories: command confirmation, projection reconciliation/repair, operator diagnostics. Routine reads issue zero Queries.

Typed failures: command-not-dispatched, `outcome_unknown_readback_unavailable`, reducer-rejected, `accepted_not_durably_projected`, projection conflict/regression, idempotent success.

## Projection Transaction Extension

`commitChangeProjection` remains canonical writer and gains:

- state-revision monotonic fence;
- operation-id/payload idempotency;
- acknowledged revision output;
- full snapshot + per-change summary-shard proof.

Under per-change lock:

1. Load current full projection and current summary pointer.
2. Same op/hash already committed → return prior acknowledged result.
3. Same op/different hash → conflict.
4. Incoming state revision below stored → reject regression.
5. Equal revision with different op/content → conflict.
6. Atomically write full snapshot.
7. Atomically write immutable summary shard for that entity/revision.
8. Atomically update only that entity's current-summary pointer.
9. Read back snapshot, shard, pointer; verify ID, revision, operation, schema, hash.
10. Return persisted/idempotent/conflict/failure.

Fire-and-forget `scheduleChangeProjection` may remain cache warming only; never satisfies command success.

## Durable Summary Index: Per-Change Shards

Do not use one shared mutable manifest under per-change locks. That would lose updates across concurrent changes.

Layout concept:

```text
summaries/
  <change-id>/
    current.json                 # small pointer, atomically replaced
    revisions/
      <state-revision>.json      # immutable summary shard
```

Properties:

- Each change writer touches only its own shard/pointer under its existing per-change lock; concurrent changes cannot overwrite one another.
- Full snapshot is committed before shard pointer. Crash can leave summary stale/missing, never ahead of snapshot truth.
- Command success requires snapshot + shard + pointer readback at acknowledged revision.
- Default list/status enumerate current pointers/shards, not full changes.
- Reader rejects malformed pointer/shard and reports typed degraded index state.
- Rebuild derives shards solely from full snapshots; no workflow Queries.
- Obsolete immutable shards are garbage-collected only after pointer and snapshot revision prove safety.

No global manifest/CAS required. A bounded aggregate launcher projection may still be regenerated from shards as a derivative cache, never authority.

## Reducer-Owned Authorization

### Single close

- Host preflight advisory only; no lifecycle disk write.
- Reducer validates authoritative lifecycle/status.
- Rejection records ledger result without state/revision change.
- Acceptance changes lifecycle, increments revision once, records accepted ledger.
- Disk write occurs only after confirmation and projection proof.

### Batch close: durable prepare/commit coordinator

Preserve current fail-all eligibility semantics across independent change workflows with a coordinator/saga, not sequential host-only prevalidation.

A durable `BatchCloseOperation` records batch ID, target IDs, reason, approvals, per-target phase/outcome, and overall state.

Protocol:

1. Coordinator sends `prepareBatchClose` with batch operation ID to every target workflow.
2. Each reducer validates lifecycle/protection and records a reservation tied to the batch ID without closing.
3. Rejected target records typed rejection. Coordinator sends `abortBatchClose` to every prepared target; no target becomes closed. Tool returns fail-all rejection after abort confirmation/projection proof.
4. If all targets prepare, coordinator persists `prepared_all`, then sends `commitBatchClose` to each.
5. Commit accepts only matching active reservation, closes once, increments revision, records ledger outcome.
6. Coordinator retries idempotently until every target is committed and projected. It does not report success while partially committed.
7. Crash recovery resumes from durable coordinator record. Replayed prepare/commit/abort is idempotent by batch ID.
8. After `prepared_all`, concurrent lifecycle commands conflicting with reservation are reducer-rejected until commit/abort resolves.

Semantics:

- **Fail-all eligibility:** any prepare rejection means zero targets close.
- **Commit convergence:** after all prepare, coordinator guarantees eventual all-target commit or remains typed in-progress/repair-required; it does not pretend cross-workflow instantaneous atomicity.
- No compensating reopen of committed close; durable coordinator prevents ambiguous success and drives convergence.

## Read Model Routing

Routine ReadStore surfaces include all workflow Query projections currently exposed by contracts/messages:

- change state/summaries;
- task list/get/ready and run summaries;
- gate status/criteria, directive, phase plan;
- acceptance/review/investment projections;
- worktree/conformance projections;
- wisdom/spec deltas;
- Epic list/show/entries;
- status/WIP/resume projections.

Rules:

- Projection present → return regardless of workflow health.
- Projection absent → typed not-found; no routine workflow hydration.
- Invalid projection → typed degraded/corrupt + repair recommendation.
- Visibility-discovered gaps are reconciliation candidates only.

Task filtering reuses existing pure helpers. Epic child joins use durable change summaries, never per-child Queries.

## Explicit Operational Exceptions

Temporal Query/Visibility allowed only behind named modules for command confirmation, reconciliation/repair, and doctor/workflow diagnostics. Structural allow-list rejects `.query(...)` elsewhere. Disk-miss routine reads cannot silently hydrate from workflow.

## Pure Metadata Boundary

Tool catalog/describe remain pure in-memory registry reads. Specs/project context/backlog remain direct filesystem/context reads.

Move filesystem helpers imported by storage readers from `temporal/activities` into a neutral filesystem module. Temporal activities may import/re-export them; pure readers cannot import `temporal/*`.

## Tier-4 Classification

- `pure`: tool catalog/describe.
- `needs-context`: specs/backlog/project context.
- `needs-read-model`: projected entity/status/WIP.
- `needs-host-probe`: git/worktree/process enrichment.
- `needs-temporal-diagnostics`: doctor/recovery only.

No Temporal probe for `needs-read-model` tools.

## Migration Sequence

1. Stable operation IDs, ledger, state revision, legacy parsing/seed handling.
2. Projection transaction fencing/idempotency + per-change summary shards.
3. ReadStore/CommandStore interfaces; old Store façade delegates temporarily.
4. Reducer close eligibility; remove pre-signal disk closure.
5. Durable batch-close coordinator with prepare/commit/abort.
6. Convert command families to projection-proof success; replace/retire direct/fire-and-forget success paths (`voidPersist`, lazy migration, content fan-out, Epic signals, archive/cancel/phase-9) or classify operationally.
7. Route all routine read projections through ReadStore.
8. Route Epic/status/WIP via snapshots + summary shards.
9. Query/writer allow-lists and Tier-4 reclassification.
10. Move pure filesystem helpers out of `temporal/*`.
11. Rebuild legacy revision-0 shards from snapshots.

## Structural Verification

- Operation properties: same ID/same payload idempotent; different payload conflict; exact-once revision.
- Projection properties: no state regression; per-change concurrent writers serialize; different-change writers preserve both summary shards; interrupted pointer publication repairs.
- Batch properties: one prepare rejection closes none; all prepare leads to eventual all commit; crash/retry idempotent; conflicting command blocked by reservation.
- Reducer authorization: stale host preflight cannot close ineligible state.
- Query/writer allow-list tests.
- Tier-4 classification and pure-boundary tests.
- Full snapshot/summary shard revision invariants.
- Worker bundle build + replay-determinism tests.

## Compatibility and Risks

- Existing Store remains temporary façade.
- Legacy state/projections default revision 0.
- Existing `_source`/`_recovery` maps to read-model provenance.
- Terminal projection dominance and SC6/no-blind-retry semantics remain.
- Command latency increases because success waits for proof; accepted tradeoff.
- Batch close becomes explicitly coordinated/eventually convergent after all-prepare, rather than pretending host-side sequential calls are atomic.
- Partial migration risk is controlled by explicit interfaces and structural allow-lists.

## Independent Concerns

Workflow retirement, Continue-As-New thresholds, dormant hibernation, and Worker Versioning rollout remain lifecycle hardening. Revision/ledger state is preserved through Continue-As-New, but retirement policy is not defined here.

# Executive Summary: Finish disk-first active reads

## Outcome

ADV now has a **projection-first CQRS-lite architecture**: routine reads resolve from schema-versioned durable disk projections and per-change summary shards with **zero Temporal workflow Query calls**, while state-changing commands carry stable operation identity, increment monotonic state revisions, and return success only after the projection is atomically committed and readback-verified. This eliminates the class of bugs where reads race with or depend on Temporal workflow health.

## Why it matters

Before this change, ADV's read path was half-flipped: some reads went through Temporal Queries, others through disk. A missing, poisoned, or orphaned workflow could block or corrupt routine reads. Command success could diverge from disk durability (the `fixDeltaAddPersistence` root cause). Lifecycle authorization depended on stale host preflight reads. This change closes those gaps structurally — not via heuristics or flags, but via typed `ReadStore`/`CommandStore` separation, projection-proof command success protocol, and reducer-owned authorization.

## What was built

- **ReadStore/CommandStore separation** (AC1, AC2): routine read tools compile against `ReadStore`; mutation tools use `CommandStore`/Temporal adapters. Structural AST tests enforce the boundary.
- **Stable operation ledger + monotonic state revision** (AC3, AC12): every behavior-changing command carries a stable `operation_id` + `payload_hash`; the workflow reducer records a bounded operation ledger and increments `state_revision` exactly once per accepted transition. Same ID/payload is idempotent; different payload is a typed conflict.
- **Projection-proof command success** (AC4): `commitChangeProjection` fences by revision/operation, atomically writes full snapshot + summary shard + pointer, readback-verifies, and returns the acknowledged revision. Injected projection failure produces typed non-blind-retry outcomes — never false success.
- **Reducer-owned lifecycle authorization** (AC5): close/closeBatch eligibility validated by the workflow reducer, not host preflight. Batch close uses a durable prepare/commit/abort coordinator with fail-all semantics.
- **Zero-Query routine reads** (AC6–AC9): `adv_change_show`, gate/task/wisdom/delta/Epic reads, default `adv_status`, and `adv_wip_state` return from the read model with zero Query calls when projection exists. Missing workflow + present projection → normal snapshot; poisoned/orphaned → degraded; missing + missing → typed not-found. Structural AST allow-list prohibits Queries outside command confirmation/reconciliation/diagnostics/repair.
- **Durable summary index** (AC8): per-change immutable summary shards under per-change locks; concurrent changes cannot overwrite each other. Default `adv_change_list` and warm `adv_status` enumerate shards, not full changes.
- **Pure metadata boundary** (AC10, AC11): tool catalog/describe remain pure in-memory; specs/context remain direct file reads. Tier-4 classification distinguishes `needs-read-model` from `needs-temporal-diagnostics`; read-model tools degrade by provenance, not failure.
- **Worker-bundle evidence** (AC13): build:worker (gen `ddc0cd03b29e`) and replay-determinism (15/15) pass; revision/reducer changes survive replay.

## Verification

- **22 new architecture test files** (194 tests) — structural AST boundary tests, behavioral zero-Query tests, projection transaction fencing, batch-close coordinator, reducer authorization, Tier-4 classification, catalog purity. All pass.
- **16 modified existing test files** — all pass, including a regression caught and fixed during verification (changes.test.ts mock wiring after reader/writer module split).
- **Worker-bundle**: build:worker `tr_ms3vbmac_14feafc4` + replay-determinism `tr_ms3v0fmk_5659228c` (15/15). Provenance recorded.
- **Spec validation**: 0 errors, 14 advisory OVERLAPPING_CAPABILITY warnings (expected — other active changes touch the same central capabilities).
- **Contract review matrix**: 30/30 items pass/respected, 0 failing.
- **Spec deltas**: 2 requirements staged (rq-projectionCommandProof01 advance-workflow, rq-projectionReadModel02 advance-meta) with 9 scenarios encoding the architecture as spec-law.

## Risks and follow-ups

- **Overlapping capabilities**: 12 other active changes also modify advance-workflow/advance-meta. Archive-time conflict resolution will be needed; the deltas are additive (new requirements, no modifications to existing).
- **External blocker resolved**: `fixDeltaAddPersistence` root cause (spec-delta signals not requesting projection) is fixed by this change's projection-proof command success. The `fixDeltaAddPersistence` change can be closed as superseded.
- **Migration**: Existing Store remains a temporary façade delegating to ReadStore/CommandStore. Legacy state/projections default to revision 0. No data migration required — projections rebuild from workflows on next signal.
- **Command latency**: Success now waits for projection proof. Accepted tradeoff per design — correctness over latency.
- **Workflow retirement** remains an independent concern (not bundled here).
